Test Description: This test verifies register-level access for the MIPI DSI subsystem across 52 registers. It performs two main validation phases: (1) Default Value Check - reads all 52 registers after reset and compares each read value against its expected default/reset value, skipping registers that are not readable based on their read mask. Any mismatch is counted as a default value failure. (2) Write/Read-Back Check - writes six distinct test data patterns to all writable registers and reads back each register to verify correctness. Registers that are flagged to be skipped or have a zero write mask are excluded from the write/read-back phase. The expected read-back value accounts for writable and readable bit fields using the read mask, write mask, and default value of each register. Any mismatch is counted as a write/read failure. A soft reset check function is defined but is not invoked in the current test flow. The test reports overall pass if zero failures are detected across both phases, and overall fail otherwise.
Test Steps / Procedure:
Step 1: Initialize failure counters for default value check and write/read check to zero.
Step 2: Execute the Default Value Check phase - iterate over all 52 MIPI DSI subsystem registers. For each register, check if the register is readable (read mask is non-zero). If not readable, skip to the next register. If readable, read the register and compare the read value against the expected default value. If a mismatch is detected, increment the default value failure counter and log the failure.
Step 3: Execute the Write/Read-Back Check phase - for each of the six test data patterns (all-ones, alternating 0xAA, alternating 0x55, all-zeros, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000), perform the following: (a) Write sub-phase: iterate over all 52 registers. Skip registers flagged in the skip list. Skip read-only registers (zero write mask). For all other registers, write the current test pattern. (b) Read-back sub-phase: iterate over all 52 registers again. Skip registers flagged in the skip list or that are read-only. Read each register and compute the expected value considering writable bits (via write mask), readable bits (via read mask), and default values for non-writable bit positions. Compare the read value against the computed expected value. If a mismatch is detected, increment the write/read failure counter and log the failure.
Step 4: Evaluate overall result - if either the default value failure counter or the write/read failure counter is greater than zero, report test FAIL. Otherwise, report test PASS.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. Default Value Verification: For each of the 52 registers, the value read after reset must exactly match the specified default value for that register. Registers with a zero read mask are excluded from this check.
2. Write/Read-Back Verification: For each of the six test data patterns written, the value read back from each writable register must match the expected value computed as: expected = (written_data AND read_mask AND write_mask) OR (inverted_write_mask AND read_mask AND default_value). Registers in the skip list or with a zero write mask are excluded.
3. Overall Pass Criteria: The test passes (finish with success) only if zero default value mismatches and zero write/read-back mismatches are detected across all registers and all test patterns. Any non-zero failure count results in test failure.
Remarks: The test covers 52 MIPI DSI subsystem registers spanning data FIFO threshold, low power, DBI, interrupt, command FIFO, pixel data FIFO, DPI control, video parameters (0-8), FIFO flush, soft control reset, DMAC configuration, DPHY TX configuration, PHY lane, PLL configuration, and DSI host registers. Six test patterns are used to exercise bit toggling coverage. A soft reset check function exists in the test but is currently not invoked. Certain registers are flagged to be skipped during the write/read-back phase. Read-only registers are automatically excluded from write operations based on their write mask.
